use_case_summary: Pilot: enterprise clinical search for multi-site health system. Primary flows: clinician free-text query -> semantic retrieval (embeddings) -> reranking for precision and hallucination reduction -> present sources with provenance. Constraints: PHI in index, per-request access logs, tenant isolation, residency requirements by state.
requirements: Index scale: target 50M-100M actionable documents; incremental updates daily
Latency: p95 query latency target <400ms for single-shot clinician queries; sub-200ms for cached/prefix queries
Cost: target blended cost per query < $0.02 at production scale; explore batching and cache strategies
Retrieval: embeddings-based ann with reranker (BERT or small cross-encoder) to improve top-5 precision
Data governance: encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, per-request audit logging retained 7 years
Networking: VPC peering or private link; no public internet egress for PHI
Authentication: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC for dataset partitions
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, request provenance in logs
Compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 required; FedRAMP discussion later
notes: Quote: "Clinicians will abandon the tool if answers take >500ms" — Director of Informatics
They currently use an in-house keyword search for EHR notes; precision last-touch is low (avg click-through 12%).
Concern: embedding storage size and reranker CPU cost for 80M docs.
SE recommended two-tier index: dense ANN + lightweight BM25 fallback for cold queries.
Raised question about legal/regulatory need for patient consent flags in index — must be able to filter by consent status.
